title: The spark's mark has four shapes: DOM plus, counter four-point star, casino diamond, glyph plus

parts.title: The spark's mark has four shapes: DOM plus, counter four-point star, casino diamond, glyph plus
parts.what: CLAUDE.md names the spark as red ✚ and the DOM coin (.spark in style.css) is an 11px plus. The canvas counter in the corner draws a vector four-point star (marks.js drawMark), the casino's bin foot draws a 5-cell diamond while its comment says it uses 'the counter's own shapes', and glyphs.js's pip spark is a 5x5 plus. On the bench screen the DOM counter and the canvas counter stand side by side with different spark shapes.
parts.proposal: The spark is a plus everywhere: one 5x5 cell bitmap (glyphs.js pip 'spark'), drawn by the counter, the casino and the DOM alike.

proposal: The spark is a plus everywhere: one 5x5 cell bitmap (glyphs.js pip 'spark'), drawn by the counter, the casino and the DOM alike.

title: The air filter's dial is a green-amber-red traffic light

parts.title: The air filter's dial is a green-amber-red traffic light
parts.what: DESIGN.md's casino section says 'Black and white, not red and green', calling a traffic-light wheel the first thing to use color for mood. Green and red already mean the farm's spores and the meteor's sparks. DIAL_ZONES paints the filter's dial #3aa655/#e2c12b/#d23b2e. The amber is in no palette, and the green and red are near-misses of the spore and spark tones.
parts.proposal: The dial reads in ink: clean/dirty/filthy as white, grey and black bands (or a SHADES ramp), never a coin color.

proposal: The dial reads in ink: clean/dirty/filthy as white, grey and black bands (or a SHADES ramp), never a coin color.

title: Yard buildings and machines are flat #000; the deep's props, plinths, domes and the finale house are grained

parts.title: Yard buildings and machines are flat #000; the deep's props, plinths, domes and the finale house are grained
parts.what: The rule says no flat fills. In the deep every built mass is hash-grained (PLINTH_TONES, DOME_TONES, props' toneAt, pods, floor), and so is the finale's house (home.js). In the yard every building is one flat #000: tower (13x34 cells, the largest mass), shack, sheds, filter, casino, houses, garage, bench, outhouse, balloons, shield props, the 'stone' arch. The machines can't be anything else, because drawSprite hardcodes '#000'/'#fff'. house.js and shack.js call the black silhouette the house grammar; apothecary.js grains its hut, but in #000-#151515, which hardly shows.
parts.proposal: Write the split down: yard buildings are flat ink silhouettes (material is dust, sky and ground only), and the finale house and apothecary follow the yard; or grain everything with one tone hook in drawSprite. Pick one.

proposal: Write the split down: yard buildings are flat ink silhouettes (material is dust, sky and ground only), and the finale house and apothecary follow the yard; or grain everything with one tone hook in drawSprite. Pick one.

title: Store screenshots are scaled 5/3 and blurred; the capsules are crisp

parts.title: Store screenshots are scaled 5/3 and blurred; the capsules are crisp
parts.what: The five store screenshots are game renders scaled by 5/3, so every 2-px rule is smeared over about 4 px with grey ramps (steamhome.png has about 4,200 colors against 29 in header_920x430.png). The press scanlines are baked in. A player comparing the capsule to the screenshots sees two renderings.
parts.proposal: Store shots are taken at an integer scale with smoothing off (and the press off); a shot has under ~100 colors.

proposal: Store shots are taken at an integer scale with smoothing off (and the press off); a shot has under ~100 colors.

title: Achievement icons repeat: whole ladders share one byte-identical picture

parts.title: Achievement icons repeat: whole ladders share one byte-identical picture
parts.what: pickOf strips the rung digits, so PEBBLE0-4 and FIRSTGRAIN are six identical icons, and ROCK0-3, CREW0-3, ORE0/1 and EVERYJOB/WHOLELOT likewise. Steam's list will show rows that look the same. The badge cell is also 16 px on a 24-px glyph cell, a second grid.
parts.proposal: Every icon unique (md5 check in steam-art); a rung carries a rung mark (pips) on the glyph's own cell.

proposal: Every icon unique (md5 check in steam-art); a rung carries a rung mark (pips) on the glyph's own cell.

title: The landing page's volume slider is the browser's default blue, round control

parts.title: The landing page's volume slider is the browser's default blue, round control
parts.what: The held sheet styles its range input (1px ink track, square paper thumb), but that rule is scoped to `.held`; title.css only sizes the slider. On the landing page's settings the volume control renders as Chrome's default blue pill with a round thumb, in light and dark alike, the one saturated non-coin color and the one rounded control on the page.
parts.proposal: Move the range rules off `.held` onto a shared selector (`.held, .col` or a `.range` class) so one slider exists.

proposal: Move the range rules off `.held` onto a shared selector (`.held, .col` or a `.range` class) so one slider exists.

title: No focus style anywhere: keyboard focus is the browser's rounded auto ring, text boxes show nothing

parts.title: No focus style anywhere: keyboard focus is the browser's rounded auto ring, text boxes show nothing
parts.what: There is no `:focus-visible` rule in any of the three sheets. Tabbing the held sheet or the landing column draws Chrome's rounded black/white auto outline (a radius in a square house), and both textareas and the cloud code input set `outline: none` with no replacement, so a focused text box looks exactly like an idle one. `body.pad :focus { outline: none }` hides even that while the pad marker is in use.
parts.proposal: One house focus rule: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 2px }` (square), applied to buttons, textareas and inputs alike.

proposal: One house focus rule: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 2px }` (square), applied to buttons, textareas and inputs alike.

title: One button height (the line-height cause)

parts.title: The same sheet button is three heights: 24px held, 27px language list, 29px landing
parts.what: `.held` sets `font: 12px var(--face)`, which resets line-height to normal, so its buttons are 24px tall (4px 14px padding). The language list re-adds `line-height: 1.4` (27px), and the landing column inherits body's 12px/1.4 plus its own `padding: 5px 14px` (29px). Measured on the live pages: settings rows 24px, language rows 27px, landing rows 29px.
parts.proposal: One `--btn-h`/line-height and one padding for every sheet button; drop the per-page line-height and the landing's 5px.

parts.title: Line-heights: normal, 1, 1.3, 1.35, 1.4, 1.5 and 13px/16px fixed
parts.what: Body is 12px/1.4, but `font: 12px var(--face)` shorthands on `.held`, toast, tip, raise, objective and modal reset to `normal`; queue and tooltip set 1.5, index text 1.5, notes 1.35 and 1.3, shelf/ledger 1, tiles 13px and tags 16px fixed. This is the root of DOM-03's three button heights.
parts.proposal: Never re-declare `font:` shorthand on a component (use `font-size`); two line-heights: 1.4 text, 1 for single-line chips.

proposal: One `--btn-h`/line-height and one padding for every sheet button; drop the per-page line-height and the landing's 5px. / Never re-declare `font:` shorthand on a component (use `font-size`); two line-heights: 1.4 text, 1 for single-line chips.

title: Purple: one accent, one ramp

parts.title: Purple means seven things: wizard magic, serpent heal, statuses on the foe, crusher fire, deep light, the gamepad cursor, the capstone rung
parts.what: config/view.js says purple is 'the only purple in the game', meaning what the wizards throw. On canvas it also marks the serpent's heal (NUM_HEAL_FACES, BAR_HEALED), every status the party lays on the foe (STATUS_FOE, including the physical Bleed and Exposed), the crusher's fire, the creatures' bioluminescence and jelly bodies, the far stream and the giant, the gamepad's selection brackets (PAD_ACCENT), and rung 8's capstone parts on deep props. So purple stands for both the enemy healing and our debuffs on it, in the same fight.
parts.proposal: Purple means magic only, on either side. Statuses on the foe and the pad cursor take ink or white, and heal-versus-debuff is told apart by shape, not hue.

parts.title: Four purple families for one meaning
parts.what: MAGIC_TONES (#9b5de5..#4e2090), ABYSS_MAGIC_TONES (12 rungs sharing only 3 of those values), the finale's FINALE_PURPLE/DARK/LIGHT (#7b3fe4, #3f2378, #b79af2, in none of the others) and the pad's PAD_ACCENT/PAD_DEEP_ACCENT (#6f36c9, #a979ef, 'the capstone purple of shelf.css') are all called 'the' purple. The finale's door and fireworks are visibly bluer than the wizards' rings beside them.
parts.proposal: One purple ramp (ABYSS_MAGIC_TONES); MAGIC_TONES, FINALE_PURPLE* and PAD_* become indices into it.

parts.title: The deep's purple accent is a literal in seven places
parts.what: `#6f36c9` (light) and `#a979ef` (dark) are written per rule in the rails: ask, cap pip, next outline, cap swatch and cap name, each with its own `html.dark` override. The `.next` outline has no dark override at all, so it stays the light purple on dark paper.
parts.proposal: `--accent` on :root with its dark value; the seven rules read it, and the missing dark `.next` comes for free.

proposal: Purple is the game's one accent (the owner, 2026-10-14: black and white for the normal, purple for anything outside it). One purple ramp in config, used everywhere purple appears; the four purple families and the literals fold into it. Open: do the coins keep green/blue/red, or go purple too?

title: A radial-gradient vignette and an alpha scanline pattern over every frame

parts.title: A radial-gradient vignette and an alpha scanline pattern over every frame
parts.what: CLAUDE.md says 'no gradients'. press.js lays a createRadialGradient vignette (PRESS_MIX.vignette 0.15) and a 1-px rgba scanline pattern over the finished frame, yard and deep alike. The scanlines put a second tone on every flat fill (rows alternate #111/#101010), and show up in every crop and in the store screenshots.
parts.proposal: Decide it explicitly: either the press is the one sanctioned gradient (written into the rules) or it goes; store shots are taken with it off.

proposal: Decide it explicitly: either the press is the one sanctioned gradient (written into the rules) or it goes; store shots are taken with it off.

title: Two number faces on the canvas: a system font at 13 px and the pixel NUM_FONT

parts.title: Two number faces on the canvas: a system font at 13 px and the pixel NUM_FONT
parts.what: Crew counts over stations, the roster's +N and hat counts, and the corner counter are fillText in the page font at 13 px (anti-aliased, off the grid). The status labels use 11 px. The deep's fight numbers and the serpent bar's level use the pixel NUM_FONT at 2 px a font pixel. A count over a shack and a blow's number are both small integers over the world, drawn in different faces.
parts.proposal: Every number drawn on the canvas uses NUM_FONT (at 2 px or at P); text labels stay DOM.

proposal: Every number drawn on the canvas uses NUM_FONT (at 2 px or at P); text labels stay DOM.

title: Large one-tone masses that are material, not buildings: the muck band, a heap's deep core, the star's crust, the cauldrons

parts.title: Large one-tone masses that are material, not buildings: the muck band, a heap's deep core, the star's crust, the cauldrons
parts.what: The muck layer can run the world's width as one MUCK_TONE body under a one-tone skin row. A dust heap thick enough to reach SHADES[5] is one flat #111 across its whole core, so the crew scene's rock reads as printed. The star's crust is one deepest red, and the apothecary's 13x10-cell cauldrons are flat sprites beside the grained hut.
parts.proposal: Any mass of material wider than ~4 cells deals its cells from two or three neighboring rungs by a hash (the PLINTH_TONES pattern), including the darkest dust rung.

proposal: Any mass of material wider than ~4 cells deals its cells from two or three neighboring rungs by a hash (the PLINTH_TONES pattern), including the darkest dust rung.

title: Shake and flash in the yard against the held-pose, no-flash/no-shake taste

parts.title: Shake and flash in the yard against the held-pose, no-flash/no-shake taste
parts.what: The owner's taste is held poses and held impacts, with no flash, shake or shudder. The yard has a full-window lightning flash, not gated on reduced motion (casino has a mayFlash gate, smog does not). It also has a shield strain shake at sin(now/42), about 3.8 Hz, in whole cells and ungated, a continuous dizzy wobble, a sine-throbbing serpent sink warning, and camera shake on casino hits, the arch catch and summons (that one gated).
parts.proposal: Impacts are held poses; any shake or flash that remains goes through one reduced-motion gate (world.js's), and the strain shake becomes held lean steps.

proposal: Impacts are held poses; any shake or flash that remains goes through one reduced-motion gate (world.js's), and the strain shake becomes held lean steps.

title: Held sheet buttons are centered; the landing column's identical buttons are left-aligned

parts.title: Held sheet buttons are centered; the landing column's identical buttons are left-aligned
parts.what: The held sheet and the landing column are built from the same markup (settings, saves, achievements, controls, language, feedback) and title.css says it is in 'the held sheet's hand', but `.held button` is `text-align: center` while `.col button` is `text-align: left`, and the headings follow suit (`.held .word` centered, `.col .word` left). The same settings page reads differently depending on where it is opened.
parts.proposal: Pick one alignment for menu buttons and page words and apply it to both `.held` and `.col` (the landing's left column can keep left only if the held sheet follows).

proposal: Pick one alignment for menu buttons and page words and apply it to both `.held` and `.col` (the landing's left column can keep left only if the held sheet follows).

title: Back rows differ page to page

parts.title: Back rows differ page to page
parts.what: Most held pages end in a full-width 'back'. The feedback page puts back and send side by side in a half-width pair inside the 26em form, narrower than the sheet. The index on a phone hides the page's back and shows its own small auto-width 'back' inside the list box, top-left. The crashed sheet has none. On the landing page back is a left-aligned row in the column.
parts.proposal: A page foot is always the sheet's width: back alone, or back + the page's action as a `.pair`; the index's inner back becomes the page's back retargeted.

proposal: A page foot is always the sheet's width: back alone, or back + the page's action as a `.pair`; the index's inner back becomes the page's back retargeted.

title: The held sheet changes width every time a page is turned

parts.title: The held sheet changes width every time a page is turned
parts.what: `.held` is sized by its content, so the sheet is 422px of buttons on the front, 190px on settings and language, 354px on saves, 396px on achievements, 312px for the feedback form. Turning a page resizes and re-centers the whole sheet. The landing column, by contrast, holds a fixed `--col-w: 21em` minimum.
parts.proposal: Give the held sheet a fixed min width (the landing's `--col-w`, shared) so pages turn in place.

proposal: Give the held sheet a fixed min width (the landing's `--col-w`, shared) so pages turn in place.

title: Selection lists come in four shapes

parts.title: Selection lists come in four shapes
parts.what: Index list: borderless rows, lowercase, 0 tracking, 2px 10px padding, inverted chosen row. Language list: bordered 27px buttons, uppercase, 4px gap, inverted chosen. Saves: bordered subgrid rows, 6px gap, inverted open row, dashed divider before the delete. Pot picker popover: borderless rows, uppercase, 4px 14px 4px 10px. The settings list sits at a 10px gap.
parts.proposal: One 'list of choices' component (row padding, gap, case, inverted chosen) for index, language, saves and the popover.

proposal: One 'list of choices' component (row padding, gap, case, inverted chosen) for index, language, saves and the popover.

title: Landing page hovers are not gated by (hover: hover) and stick after a tap

parts.title: Landing page hovers are not gated by (hover: hover) and stick after a tap
parts.what: Every hover in style.css is inside `@media (hover: hover)`, but title.css's `.col button:hover`, `.col button.play:hover`, `.foot a:hover` and `.foot .cloud .go:hover` are bare, so on a phone the tapped button stays inverted (and play flips to paper) until something else is tapped.
parts.proposal: Wrap the landing hovers in `@media (hover: hover)` as style.css does.

proposal: Wrap the landing hovers in `@media (hover: hover)` as style.css does.

title: A shelf tile's gain is clipped with an ellipsis, against the card rule

parts.title: A shelf tile's gain is clipped with an ellipsis, against the card rule
parts.what: style.css says what a row gives 'is never truncated', and the card's gain wraps. On a shelf the same `.gain` is `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` on one line, so 'wizards that light...' loses its words on the bench.
parts.proposal: Let the shelf gain wrap to two lines (as `.locked` already does) and drop the ellipsis.

proposal: Let the shelf gain wrap to two lines (as `.locked` already does) and drop the ellipsis.

title: Three card anatomies for one 'thing you can buy'

parts.title: Three card anatomies for one 'thing you can buy'
parts.what: style.css cards (name, pips top-right, gain, bill, time, note in a 2-column grid, 1px border, invert on hover), shelf tiles (glyph, name, gain, boxed tag, vertical pips, borderless, lift on hover) and the rails' `.rl-row` (bold title, 13px subtitle, its own tag, 1px border) each carry name, price and pips differently. The objective's barrier buy is a fourth (3px double border, centered bill).
parts.proposal: Write the card anatomy once (name, price tag, pips, state) and make shelf/rails variants of it, starting with the price tag box.

proposal: Write the card anatomy once (name, price tag, pips, state) and make shelf/rails variants of it, starting with the price tag box.

title: Fading: by tone down the ramp, not by alpha

parts.title: Yard alpha fades make off-palette pastels; the deep forbids alpha
parts.what: rift.js says 'There is no alpha here: a thing fades by being painted in a darker tone of its own family', and the deep keeps that rule. The yard fades by globalAlpha: about 80 sites in sky.js, smog.js, cores.js, crew.js and tower.js, plus the cutscene recede at 35% ink. The results are lavender rings around the tower, pale green and pale blue heaps under the finale, and grey-tinted crew. None of these tones is in any palette.
parts.proposal: A fade steps down its own palette ramp (as in the deep); globalAlpha only for the press and cutscene veils.

parts.title: The deep's 'no alpha, fade down the ramp' rule is broken by its own HUD and bodies
parts.what: rift.js, arms.js, cores.js:97 and riftlife.js all say there is no alpha. Yet globalAlpha fades the serpent's sink veil, fighters and swimmers (bodyInk), deep motes, fight numbers, the whole serpent bar with its heal and shards, and the rift's own twinkle and rings in cores.js, against its own comment. The fight numbers alone fade three ways on one screen: quantized alpha for blows, tone faces plus a 0.5-alpha pop for heals, continuous alpha for bar shards.
parts.proposal: In the deep every fade is a ramp step (ABYSS_TONES / ABYSS_MAGIC_TONES); alpha is reserved for whole-screen veils.

parts.title: Things in the same sky fade two ways: clouds by tone, balloons by alpha
parts.what: Clouds and rain fade toward the page by mixing tones (weather.js paled(), exported 'for anything in the sky that is not a cloud'). Balloons and their plumes, at the same depth and on the same fadeAt, use globalAlpha. Balloons also move eased and off-lattice in play, but in held steps in the finale.
parts.proposal: Everything in the sky fades through paled(); balloons move on whole cells.

proposal: A fade steps down its own palette ramp (as in the deep); globalAlpha only for the press and cutscene veils. / In the deep every fade is a ramp step (ABYSS_TONES / ABYSS_MAGIC_TONES); alpha is reserved for whole-screen veils. / Everything in the sky fades through paled(); balloons move on whole cells.

title: Coin colors: tokens, dark mode, and the tonics

parts.title: Coin colors are hex literals repeated across two sheets, with no tokens
parts.what: Ore blue `#2f5fd0`, spark red `#d93a25` and crop green `#2e9e4b` are written in the coin marks and again in the ladder pip bands (style.css) and again in shelf.css, eleven literals in all, with no `--coin-*` token and no dark-mode variant.
parts.proposal: `--coin-ore`, `--coin-crop`, `--coin-spark` on :root (with dark values) and every literal replaced.

parts.title: Ore blue on dark paper is below 3:1
parts.what: The coin colors do not change in dark mode. `#2f5fd0` on `--paper #1f1f1f` is about 2.9:1 (red about 3.6:1), so the ore triangle and the blue ladder pips sink into the board in dark mode, while the deep's purple accent does get a lighter dark variant.
parts.proposal: Lighter dark-mode coin values under `html.dark` (as the rails' `#a979ef` does) once the tokens of DOM-23 exist.

parts.title: Tonic colors are near-duplicates of the coin colors, outside FIND_COLOR
parts.what: The three tonics are tinted #5fb84f, #4a86c7 and #e04848, each a step off its coin's FIND_COLOR ramp (#57c074, #3f68d4/#5b83e0, #e8503a) and in no palette. The fire's fallback is an orange #f5851f that exists nowhere else. On the apothecary the brew reads as a fourth, paler green next to the farm's spores.
parts.proposal: A tonic takes its reagent coin's FIND_COLOR ramp (tonicColor = FIND_COLOR[coin][k]); no tonic literals and no orange.

proposal: `--coin-ore`, `--coin-crop`, `--coin-spark` on :root (with dark values) and every literal replaced. / Lighter dark-mode coin values under `html.dark` (as the rails' `#a979ef` does) once the tokens of DOM-23 exist. / A tonic takes its reagent coin's FIND_COLOR ramp (tonicColor = FIND_COLOR[coin][k]); no tonic literals and no orange.

title: Greys: one ramp, one muted text tone, one black

parts.title: Five grey ramps, with near-duplicates one or two steps apart in the same role
parts.what: The yard's greys are SHADES (#8a8a8a..#111111). Beside them sit FINALE_GREYS ('the yard's greys by name', but #262626..#e3e3e3, none equal to SHADES), the abyss's blue-tinted ABYSS_TONES, AIR_TINTS dust, PAPER, and one-off greys. The one-offs include a mid-grey cluster all meaning 'empty/inactive': #8a8a8a (PORTAL_TORN), #8c8c8c (SEAT_EMPTY_INK, SHELF_INK short), #8f8f8f (HOUSE_CURTAIN) and #909090 (CLOUD_UNDER). Also #a4a4a4 (rain) next to #a6a6a6 (air dust), #aaa (float shadow), #bdbdbd (build ghost), and #3a3a3a (apothecary smoke) next to finale #3d3d3d.
parts.proposal: One yard grey ramp (SHADES extended to paper, about 8 rungs); every grey on the yard canvas is a SHADES index, and the deep keeps ABYSS_TONES as its own.

parts.title: Muted text uses three different greys for the same role
parts.what: Secondary text is `--ink-2` on the landing tagline, sub-label and foot, `--ink-4` for achievement notes, shelf gains and the rails reset, and `--ink-5` for ledger notes and empty lines; `--ink-7` is the toast note. Cards instead mute with `opacity: .7/.72/.75`. Five treatments for 'quieter text'.
parts.proposal: One `--muted` token for secondary text (ink-4), ink-5 kept for disabled only, and no opacity muting.

parts.title: Buildings are #000, the deepest dust is #111: two blacks for mass
parts.what: A heap's deepest dust is SHADES[5] #111111, one flat tone, while every building, the bench and the pot are pure #000. Where a heap stands against a building (the crew scene's rock beside the shack) the two blacks meet with no reason.
parts.proposal: The darkest dust shade is #000 or buildings are SHADES[5]; one black for mass.

proposal: One yard grey ramp (SHADES extended to paper, about 8 rungs); every grey on the yard canvas is a SHADES index, and the deep keeps ABYSS_TONES as its own. / One `--muted` token for secondary text (ink-4), ink-5 kept for disabled only, and no opacity muting. / The darkest dust shade is #000 or buildings are SHADES[5]; one black for mass.

title: Headings and label case

parts.title: Labels drop to lowercase in some places and not others
parts.what: The rule mostly reads 'names and labels upper, sentences lower'. Breaking it: the books ledger's row labels ('pebbles', 'ore', 'playtime') are lowercase and untracked; the index list's names are lowercase; the crew window's section 'the yard' is lowercase (the modal sets no case, so `.rows .sect` inherits none); the mess tags say 'muck'/'poop' lowercase under an uppercase toast name; shelf tags say 'done' and gains 'queued' lowercase.
parts.proposal: Write the case rule down (label = upper + track, sentence = lower + 0) and set case on the component, not by inheritance.

parts.title: Section headings are drawn four ways
parts.what: Board page title: 12px, .18em, regular, 2px ink rule under. Shelf section sign: 12px bold .18em, inverted ink block, 5px plank above. Ledger section: 12px bold .18em, 1px ink rule under. Rows section in the crew window: inherited case, 1px ink-5 (grey) rule. The modal head title is a fifth: 12px .3em, no rule.
parts.proposal: Two heading levels only: page title (regular, rule) and section (bold, rule or sign, one choice), shared by boards, ledger and windows.

proposal: Write the case rule down (label = upper + track, sentence = lower + 0) and set case on the component, not by inheritance. / Two heading levels only: page title (regular, rule) and section (bold, rule or sign, one choice), shared by boards, ledger and windows.

title: Line weights and outlines: one rule

parts.title: Board outlines straddle their edge in one place and inset in another
parts.what: Bodies, carts and the count card stroke 2 px inset by 1 px (strokeRect(x+1, y+1, w-2, h-2)), so the rule lies inside the box on whole pixels. Progress bars and both casino boards stroke max(1, P/3) centered on the edge, so half the rule falls outside the box and the outer edge is 1 px off the lattice. Same 2-px rule, two placements.
parts.proposal: A 2-px rule always lies inside its box (inset 1 with lineWidth 2), never centered on the edge.

parts.title: Hairline widths disagree: 1 px ghost and hold ring vs 2 px everywhere else
parts.what: In the yard the de-facto thin line is 2 px (ladder rails, antenna, tape, sight ring, ground line). The build ghost outline is P/6 = 1 px (bars.js EDGE) while the tint stroke beside it is P/3, and the hold ring is a 1-px white hairline at +0.5. On the shelf both ghost and tint are 1 px at a 3-px cell, so the yard glyph has different proportions from the same glyph on the card. The rift ring is configured as 2 'screen px' but drawn in world px and half clipped.
parts.proposal: The thinnest line in the world is P/3 (2 px); 1 px only on screen-space UI rims.

parts.title: Border weights: overlays are 1px or 2px with no rule for which
parts.what: The held sheet, landing column, tooltip and toast are 1px; the board sheet, modal, purse, queue, objective, corner buttons, hop, popover, raise and build button are 2px. The modal's close button is 2px while every button inside a sheet is 1px. Emphasis uses 3px double (goal card, barrier buy) and 3px solid (shelf goal), two ways of saying the same thing.
parts.proposal: Rule it: 2px = something floating over the yard, 1px = a control or a line inside it; one emphasis border (3px double) for goal cards everywhere.

parts.title: Stroked arcs and diagonals in a cell-stepped world: sky ring, benched disc, bridge ramps, casino lever, kit pips
parts.what: Most rings and diagonals are stepped in cells: flag waves, tower rings, sphere halo, ram wheel, belt ramp, shield braces, filter needle. A few use canvas strokes and arcs that anti-alias: the benched star's skyRing (2 px arc, despite the file's own note that a stroked line would be the only stroke in the sky), the benched disc (filled arc), the bridge ramps (2 px diagonal), the casino lever (a P-wide diagonal stroke) and the kit pips (round arcs, where the serpent bar's pips are square).
parts.proposal: No ctx.arc or diagonal stroke in the world: rings and slopes are cells (the kit's ring() helper and the belt ramp's steps are the models); the rift's deliberate arc stars stay as the one written exception.

parts.title: The pile-full warning triangle is the one anti-aliased, hollow, fractional mark over a station
parts.what: warning() draws a vector triangle with a stroke r/6 = 2.6 px and a bar and dot sized r/8, r/4 and 0.35r (WARN_R = P*2.6), so every edge blurs and nothing sits on the cell grid. Every other over-station mark (done tick, building glyph, deep choose mark) is solid cells on the grid. style.css copies the r/6 stroke for the .messtag tags.
parts.proposal: The warning mark is a cell bitmap like the other station marks (a hollow 2-px-ruled triangle of whole cells).

proposal: A 2-px rule always lies inside its box (inset 1 with lineWidth 2), never centered on the edge. / The thinnest line in the world is P/3 (2 px); 1 px only on screen-space UI rims. / Rule it: 2px = something floating over the yard, 1px = a control or a line inside it; one emphasis border (3px double) for goal cards everywhere. / No ctx.arc or diagonal stroke in the world: rings and slopes are cells (the kit's ring() helper and the belt ramp's steps are the models); the rift's deliberate arc stars stay as the one written exception. / The warning mark is a cell bitmap like the other station marks (a hollow 2-px-ruled triangle of whole cells).

title: The same kind of motion done several ways

parts.title: A creature flinching from a hit moves three ways
parts.what: The serpent's dent is held whole-cell steps. A creature the player clicks eases through a Hermite cubic with a smoothstep blend, and the same creature scared by a lash steps in held floor(age*rate) frames. Whether a creature is touched by a click or a lash changes the animation grammar, not just the reaction.
parts.proposal: Reactions to a blow are held poses with a smear (the serpent's grammar); eased motion only for travel.

parts.title: Five hops, five motion styles
parts.what: The landing hop is a continuous parabola and the yard dance a continuous |sin|. The finale crowd hops on a held pose table, the abyss-intro hop is a two-state toggle, and the deep-rest hop is physics with drag. A body jumping for joy reads differently in each place it does it.
parts.proposal: A crew hop is one held pose table (the finale's), shared by the dance, the landing and the rest.

parts.title: The serpent's jaw opens four ways
parts.what: Meal bite: smoothstep. Snatch head: an inline smoothstep. Roar: linear. Recoil: a held smear and pose. They are the same mouth on the same creature.
parts.proposal: The jaw has one held pose table (shut, ajar, gape) every caller steps through.

parts.title: Easing and step helpers copied about 20 times with different curves under one name
parts.what: smoothstep k*k*(3-2k) is written out at about 14 sites, some clamped and some not. Only deep/kits.js exports one. Quad in-out, out-cubic and lerp each have 4-7 copies, and `ease` names a quad in deep/rest.js but an out-cubic in cutscene.js. The held-step quantizers come in six variants mixing floor and ceil, and two different functions are both called stepOf.
parts.proposal: One motion module (smoothstep, outCubic, quadInOut, lerp, held(t, steps)) imported everywhere; a held step is floor.

proposal: Reactions to a blow are held poses with a smear (the serpent's grammar); eased motion only for travel. / A crew hop is one held pose table (the finale's), shared by the dance, the landing and the rest. / The jaw has one held pose table (shut, ajar, gape) every caller steps through. / One motion module (smoothstep, outCubic, quadInOut, lerp, held(t, steps)) imported everywhere; a held step is floor.

title: Off the cell grid: half-cell edges and sizes

parts.title: Half-cell eaves, chimney caps and roof lips put 3-px hairlines on the buildings
parts.what: SHACK_EAVE is P/2, and house.js hangs eaves P/2 past the wall at P/2 tall, with a chimney cap offset P/2. At the device pixel ratio the 3-px lip anti-aliases into a grey edge, visible in the shot as a grey line over the house roof. Everything else on the building is whole cells.
parts.proposal: Lips and eaves are a whole cell (P) or none; nothing on a building is a fraction of P.

parts.title: Off-grid cell sizes: P-1 'comic' marks, a 1.5-cell mooring stake, half-cell basket weave
parts.what: Crew speech marks (dizzy stars, swear bursts) are P-1 squares at P/2 offsets, so they sit between cells. The balloon's mooring stake is P*1.5 wide, and the basket's weave is P/2 tall. The rest of the crew and balloon sit on whole cells.
parts.proposal: Every fillRect is a whole number of cells at a cell-snapped origin; a gap between marks is a skipped cell, not P-1.

parts.title: The deep's giant is drawn on half cells as a flat smooth-edged lozenge
parts.what: The giant crossing behind the deep is a flat PURPLES[1] fill. Its cell is P*zoom*0.5 and its outline is a sine with hand constants (len 320, r 34, 0.6, 1.2, 6), so its edge reads smooth beside the cell-grid creatures and is one flat tone. That breaks both the grid and the per-cell variation rule. The far stream also uses its own smaller farCell.
parts.proposal: Far things are drawn on the same cell at a darker ramp rung, with hash-dealt tones; depth is tone, not a finer grid.

parts.title: Off-grid continuous drift on things that are otherwise cell-snapped
parts.what: The glyph stacks over stations drift by two summed sines in whole yard pixels (BUILD_DRIFT 2), so they sit up to ±4 px off the 6-px lattice. The cursor motes spin per rendered frame (not per dt) and off the grid. The noticeboard pops in at the first banked grain with no fade, and the serpent bar's phase boxes appear one by one with no fade while the bar itself fades.
parts.proposal: Drift moves a whole cell on a held beat; spins step by dt; nothing appears without a fade or a build.

proposal: Lips and eaves are a whole cell (P) or none; nothing on a building is a fraction of P. / Every fillRect is a whole number of cells at a cell-snapped origin; a gap between marks is a skipped cell, not P-1. / Far things are drawn on the same cell at a darker ramp rung, with hash-dealt tones; depth is tone, not a finer grid. / Drift moves a whole cell on a held beat; spins step by dt; nothing appears without a fade or a build.

title: How "on", chosen and disabled look

parts.title: Toggle rows have four different 'on' languages
parts.what: Settings toggles say their state in words ('dark: off') with no visual state; the language list marks the chosen row by inverting it; the feedback form uses a 12px checkbox with an inset square; 'hide finished' goes from dashed to solid border and from .7 to full opacity. Four mechanisms for 'this is on'.
parts.proposal: Decide one toggle anatomy (word plus a box tick on the right, or inversion for 'on') and use it for settings, hide finished and the feedback tick.

parts.title: Four different tick boxes
parts.what: The feedback tick is a 12px box, 1px border, 2px-inset fill. The objective's quest list uses text glyphs '\u25a1'/'\u25a0' in the 11px face. The barrier bill uses a 7px box with a 1px inset that fades in. The landing foot's cloud mark is a 6px filled/hollow square. None share size, stroke or fill inset.
parts.proposal: One `.tickbox` (size in em so it rides the text size, 1px stroke, fixed inset) used by the form, the quest list and the bill.

parts.title: Disabled is written three ways, and not at all on the landing page
parts.what: Board cards go `--ink-5` and dashed; shelf tags dashed and ink-5; the barrier buy ink-5 border; the feedback tick and send drop to `opacity: .4`; the rails' locked arm to `.45`; the dev panel to `.4`. `.col button:disabled` only changes the cursor, so a disabled landing button looks live.
parts.proposal: Disabled = `color: var(--ink-5)` + dashed border, for every control; drop the opacity variants and give `.col` the same.

parts.title: Hover is inversion almost everywhere, except shelves, toasts and a few one-offs
parts.what: Sheet buttons, cards, popover rows, queue rows, raise, modal close and barrier buttons invert on hover. Shelf tiles instead lift with a 1px offset shadow and sway; 'hide finished' and the save delete fade (.7); the toast inverts back to paper; footer links only darken the underline. The inversion is the rule; these are exceptions that are not written down.
parts.proposal: Write hover = invert as the rule and keep the shelf lift as the one documented exception; bring the delete and hide-finished into it.

parts.title: Pressed state exists only on phone board cards
parts.what: `:active` inversion is defined once, for `.rows button` inside the phone media block. Sheet buttons, landing buttons, shelf tiles and popover rows have no pressed state on any device; on desktop the hover already inverts so it is moot, on touch it is the only feedback a tap gets.
parts.proposal: One `:active:not(:disabled)` inversion for every button, so touch gets the same feedback everywhere.

proposal: Decide one toggle anatomy (word plus a box tick on the right, or inversion for 'on') and use it for settings, hide finished and the feedback tick. / One `.tickbox` (size in em so it rides the text size, 1px stroke, fixed inset) used by the form, the quest list and the bill. / Disabled = `color: var(--ink-5)` + dashed border, for every control; drop the opacity variants and give `.col` the same. / Write hover = invert as the rule and keep the shelf lift as the one documented exception; bring the delete and hide-finished into it. / One `:active:not(:disabled)` inversion for every button, so touch gets the same feedback everywhere.

title: Store capsules: the tool's own palette and details

parts.title: Capsule palette and title font are the tool's own, not the game's
parts.what: The capsules use warm off-whites and near-blacks (#f6f6f4 paper, #efefec earth, #e1e1dd hatch, #141414 ink, #cfc9c4 spray, warm cloud greys) found nowhere in src, where the game is #fff/#000 and neutral SHADES. The title is a private 5x7 bitmap font with a serifed I that the game never shows (in-game the name is DOM monospace text). Its letter cells are 13-20 px, not whole multiples of P. The capsule rock is three concentric noisy bands with no #000 core, unlike the game's depth-shaded rock.
parts.proposal: steam-art imports every color from src/config and shades the rock with depthShade; one title drawing lives in src and both the title page and the capsules use it.

parts.title: Capsule details break yard rules: clipped clouds, floating crew, half-cell rock steps
parts.what: The title knockout is painted over the clouds, leaving straight cut edges. About 30% of the crest crew stand a cell above the rock. The icon rock's (16-w)/2*u centering puts odd-width rows on half cells, which anti-alias (#858584 in small_462x174.png). The hero is drawn at c=12, a second scale.
parts.proposal: Capsules obey the yard: nothing floats, nothing is cut, no fractional fillRect, one cell size scaled by whole numbers.

proposal: steam-art imports every color from src/config and shades the rock with depthShade; one title drawing lives in src and both the title page and the capsules use it. / Capsules obey the yard: nothing floats, nothing is cut, no fractional fillRect, one cell size scaled by whole numbers.

title: A type scale: sizes, letter-spacing, bold

parts.title: Eleven letter-spacing values
parts.what: Tracking in use: .04em (phone controls), .06em (phone boards), .08em (tip, queue, tile names, ledger labels), .1em (cards, small print), .12em (toast name), .14em (held/landing buttons, raise), .18em (page titles, section signs), .22em (pips), .25em (cloud head), .3em (page words, modal title, pair code), .34em (game name), plus raw `.3em`/`.04em` not multiplied by `--track`. Small print inherits px tracking from its parent, so `.held .small` computes to .168em.
parts.proposal: Four tracking steps as tokens (`--track-0: 0`, `--track-s: .08em`, `--track-m: .14em`, `--track-l: .3em`), always multiplied by `--track`.

parts.title: Five 'small' sizes: 9.84px, 10px, 10.2px, 10.8px, 11px
parts.what: Small print is written five ways: `.82em` (page notes, pot-picker notes = 9.84px), `10px` (held .small, landing sub/said/foot, objective 'next' tab, skip), `.85em` (shelf tile names, strip = 10.2px), `.9em` (card notes = 10.8px), `11px` (record, quest list, barrier, ledger notes). The measured sweep confirms all five on screen.
parts.proposal: A three-step scale (10px small, 12px body, 17px word, with 14px display) as tokens; replace the em fractions with the token.

parts.title: Display sizes 14, 15, 17, 18, 34px with no ladder between them
parts.what: Index entry name 14px, shelf goal name 14px bold, toast name 15px, page word 17px, pairing code 18px, game name 34px; the rails' private `--rl-text: 13px`/`--rl-head: 14px`/`--rl-tiny: 12px` add a 13px body nowhere else uses.
parts.proposal: Fold 14/15 into one 'name' size and 17/18 into the 'word' size; retire the rails' 13px body for the house 12px.

parts.title: Bold appears in shelf/ledger headings and the barrier name, nowhere else
parts.what: Weight 700 is used for the shelf section sign, the ledger section, the shelf goal name, the objective barrier name, the rails and the controller glyphs. Board page titles, modal titles, held words and toast names stay regular, so 'heading' is bold on one board and regular on the next.
parts.proposal: Bold for section level only (DOM-13), regular for page titles and names.

proposal: Four tracking steps as tokens (`--track-0: 0`, `--track-s: .08em`, `--track-m: .14em`, `--track-l: .3em`), always multiplied by `--track`. / A three-step scale (10px small, 12px body, 17px word, with 14px display) as tokens; replace the em fractions with the token. / Fold 14/15 into one 'name' size and 17/18 into the 'word' size; retire the rails' 13px body for the house 12px. / Bold for section level only (DOM-13), regular for page titles and names.

title: A red/cyan chromatic fringe on rising motes, against the press's own reasoning

parts.title: A red/cyan chromatic fringe on rising motes, against the press's own reasoning
parts.what: press.js says chromatic aberration was left out because it is 'a fringe the whole pixel discipline exists to prevent'. render/smog.js draws exactly that fringe on the climbing plume motes toward the screen edges, in #c02a2a and #1f9ad0. Both colors are in no palette, and the red reads as a spark.
parts.proposal: No color fringes: motes are drawn in their SMOG_TINTS tone only (HAZE_CA = 0).

proposal: No color fringes: motes are drawn in their SMOG_TINTS tone only (HAZE_CA = 0).

title: Coin marks drawn as anti-aliased vector shapes at 9 px, off the cell

parts.title: Coin marks drawn as anti-aliased vector shapes at 9 px, off the cell
parts.what: The counter's marks are 9-px vector triangles, hexagons and stars with paths (moveTo/lineTo), so they blur at their edges, and 9 is 1.5 cells. Out in the yard the same coins are whole-cell squares, and in the casino 5-cell bitmaps.
parts.proposal: Coin marks are bitmaps (the glyphs.js 5x5 pips) drawn at whole pixels; no vector paths for marks.

proposal: Coin marks are bitmaps (the glyphs.js 5x5 pips) drawn at whole pixels; no vector paths for marks.

title: Colors outside the tokens in DOM chrome

parts.title: Colors outside the tokens in DOM chrome
parts.what: `#objective.deep` hard-codes `#000`/`#fff`/`#5f5f66` (the only blue-grey in the game). The dotted page texture is a data-URI written five times with `%23000` and three more with `%23e0e0e0` for dark, instead of reading `--ink`. The scrim is `rgb(0 0 0 / .4)` with white dots in both modes. A shelf tile's resting border is `rgba(0,0,0,0)`. cards.html hard-codes `#fff` and `#555`.
parts.proposal: Dot pattern as one `--dots` custom property set per mode; `#5f5f66` to `--ink-7`; cards.html on the tokens.

proposal: Dot pattern as one `--dots` custom property set per mode; `#5f5f66` to `--ink-7`; cards.html on the tokens.

title: The cards bench has no dark mode

parts.title: The cards bench has no dark mode
parts.what: cards.html sets `body { background: #fff }` and `h2 { color: #555 }` and does not load the pre-paint dark script, so `?dark` renders dark-mode cards on a white page and a card's dark look cannot be checked on the bench.
parts.proposal: Bench on `var(--paper)`/`var(--ink-4)` and honor `?dark` like play.html.

proposal: Bench on `var(--paper)`/`var(--ink-4)` and honor `?dark` like play.html.

title: Separator in setting labels: colon for toggles, middle dot for pages

parts.title: Separator in setting labels: colon for toggles, middle dot for pages
parts.what: Settings rows read 'motion: full', 'dark: off', 'sound: on' but 'language · english'; the front reads 'saves · 0 of 3'. The dot means 'opens a page with this value'; the colon means 'press to flip'. The rule is unwritten, and the words are the owner's to change.
parts.proposal: Ask the owner to confirm the rule (colon = toggle, dot = door) and write it into the rules; pair with DOM-05.

proposal: Ask the owner to confirm the rule (colon = toggle, dot = door) and write it into the rules; pair with DOM-05.

title: Radii: round pips, round clock, rounded controller glyphs in a square house

parts.title: Radii: round pips, round clock, rounded controller glyphs in a square house
parts.what: The ladder pips (cards, tiles, rails) and the clock mark are circles; the controller glyphs use `border-radius: 50%` and `.35em`. These are glyph-level and arguably deliberate, but the pips are the one round shape on every card and the shelf's queued pip draws its dot with a gradient.
parts.proposal: Write down that pips, the clock and pad glyphs are the only round shapes; everything else stays square.

proposal: Write down that pips, the clock and pad glyphs are the only round shapes; everything else stays square.

title: Tracking tightens on phone for boards and controls only

parts.title: Tracking tightens on phone for boards and controls only
parts.what: Below 560px the board sheet and cards drop to .06em and the controls page to .04em, but the held sheet's buttons, the landing column and the toasts keep .14em, so a phone shows two trackings side by side.
parts.proposal: Tighten by changing `--track` once on phone instead of per component.

proposal: Tighten by changing `--track` once on phone instead of per component.

title: Landing foot sits 36px from the left and 18px from the right

parts.title: Landing foot sits 36px from the left and 18px from the right
parts.what: `.foot { left: 36px; right: 18px }`, while the column above it stands 20px in. The build line does not align with the column's edge or mirror the links.
parts.proposal: Foot on the column's 20px (`--edge`-based) margins on both sides.

proposal: Foot on the column's 20px (`--edge`-based) margins on both sides.

title: CJK language rows render larger than their neighbors

parts.title: CJK language rows render larger than their neighbors
parts.what: Each language is in its own face; the Chinese and Korean names come out visibly larger and heavier than the Latin rows in the same list (the `Pit SC/KR` fallbacks at 12px), so the list looks uneven.
parts.proposal: Size the CJK faces with `size-adjust` (or a per-lang font-size) to the Latin face's x-height.

proposal: Size the CJK faces with `size-adjust` (or a per-lang font-size) to the Latin face's x-height.

title: The story card's deep variant ignores dark mode

parts.title: The story card's deep variant ignores dark mode
parts.what: `#objective.deep` pins `--paper: #000; --ink: #fff`, so in dark mode the deep card is pure black on a #1f1f1f page, and in light it is a black card among white ones; its shadow tone `#5f5f66` is off the grey ramp.
parts.proposal: Deep card = the inverted tokens (`--paper: var(--ink)`) so it inverts correctly in both modes.

proposal: Deep card = the inverted tokens (`--paper: var(--ink)`) so it inverts correctly in both modes.

title: Index on a phone: inner back button, no page back

parts.title: Index on a phone: inner back button, no page back
parts.what: On a phone the index pushes the entry over the list and shows `.ixback`, an auto-width button inside the bordered index box, while hiding the sheet's own full-width back. Every other phone page keeps its back at the foot.
parts.proposal: Keep the page's back at the foot and retarget it to 'list' while an entry is open.

proposal: Keep the page's back at the foot and retarget it to 'list' while an entry is open.

title: The same component written twice

parts.title: The badge is defined twice, and inverts the other way on shelves
parts.what: `.rows .sect .badge` and `.page .title .badge` are identical rules written twice; on a shelf the section badge reverses to paper-on-ink inside an inverted sign. The 'new' corner is likewise drawn twice at two sizes (a 10px solid triangle on cards, a 4px bordered one on tiles).
parts.proposal: One `.badge` and one `.new` corner rule, sized in em.

parts.title: The cloud section, textarea and veil are each written twice, for .held and .col
parts.what: `.held .cloudsheet` and `.col .cloudsheet` repeat border, padding, head tracking, pair-code size and input styling; the textarea rules are duplicated; `.veil` is defined in both sheets with different z-index (20 vs 9) and duration (.45s vs .35s), and the landing loads both so the later wins.
parts.proposal: One `.cloudsheet`/`textarea`/`.veil` rule set unscoped; the landing keeps only its layout differences.

parts.title: Toast and mess tags: same bar, different hand
parts.what: The toast and mess tags share the ink fill, 1px paper border plus 1px ink outline and the float shadow, but the toast name is 15px uppercase tracked and the mess tag label 12px lowercase untracked, and the skip button (same chrome) is 10px. Three dark bars, three type treatments.
parts.proposal: One 'dark chip' label style (12px upper .1em) for mess tags and skip; the toast name stays the one display size.

proposal: One `.badge` and one `.new` corner rule, sized in em. / One `.cloudsheet`/`textarea`/`.veil` rule set unscoped; the landing keeps only its layout differences. / One 'dark chip' label style (12px upper .1em) for mess tags and skip; the toast name stays the one display size.

title: A spacing scale: gaps and paddings

parts.title: Gaps between stacked controls: 4, 6, 7 and 10px
parts.what: Held sheet stack 10px; landing column 7px; language list 4px; saves rows 6px; record cards 6px; board cards `--rows-gap` 4px; board sheet 6px; pairs 10px. The spacing tokens `--gap` 8px and `--pad-s/m/l` exist but no stack uses `--gap`.
parts.proposal: Two stack gaps (tight 4px inside a list, loose 8px between controls) as tokens; use them everywhere.

parts.title: Button paddings are hand-cut per component
parts.what: Held 4px 14px; landing 5px 14px; cards 6px 8px (6px 3px on phone); queue 1px 12px; popover 4px 14px 4px 10px; tip 3px 6px; hide finished 2px 6px (6px 8px on phone); modal close 0 6px; barrier buy 2px 6px; cancel 1px 6px; dev 0 4px. Only the tip, toast, raise, objective, modal and skip use the `--pad-s/m/l` tokens.
parts.proposal: Map every control to `--pad-s` or `--pad-m` and delete the literals.

parts.title: The float shadow is on some floating panels and not others
parts.what: `--float-shadow` sits under the corner buttons, toast, queue, objective, modal, raise, build button, skip and mess tags, but not under the board sheet, the purse beside it, the held sheet or the tooltip, which float over the same yard.
parts.proposal: Every 2px floating panel gets the shadow, or none of the large ones do; write which.

proposal: Two stack gaps (tight 4px inside a list, loose 8px between controls) as tokens; use them everywhere. / Map every control to `--pad-s` or `--pad-m` and delete the literals. / Every 2px floating panel gets the shadow, or none of the large ones do; write which.
